title: Gorkha Kingdom
capsule: The Kingdom of Gorkha was one of the Chaubisi Rajya (twenty-four principalities) of the western hills of Nepal, founded by Dravya Shah in 1559 from the small hill fort of Gorkha. For two centuries it remained a minor chieftaincy squeezed between Kathmandu Valley kingdoms and rival hill states, but under Prithvi Narayan Shah (r. 1743–1775) it launched a systematic campaign of conquest that by 1768 had captured Kathmandu, Patan, and Bhaktapur. That conquest transformed Gorkha from a regional polity into the nucleus of a unified Nepal; Prithvi Narayan Shah moved his capital to Kathmandu, effectively ending Gorkha's existence as a distinct kingdom and inaugurating the Shah dynasty's rule over Nepal.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core territory around Gorkha town is well established; the precise extent of tributary or seasonally controlled lands in the pre-1743 period is only loosely documented in hill chronicles (vamsavalis).
